title: The EDGE-CALIFA Survey: Molecular Gas and Star Formation Activity across the Green Valley
question: How do star formation quenching processes along the main sequence, green valley and red cloud change the molecular gas fraction and star formation efficiency (SFE_mol = SFR/M_mol), globally and as a function of radius, in massive nearby galaxies?

recipe.method: Image observatory-calibrated uv data with the PHANGS-ALMA imaging pipeline (common spectral grid, continuum subtraction, multi-scale then single-scale clean, round beam, Kelvin units)
key_parameters: channel width 5.08 km/s, LSR, radio definition
multi-scale clean scales 0, 5, 10 arcsec, S/N ~ 4 threshold

recipe.method: Combine (logical OR) a CO-based dilated mask with the best of three independent masks (Halpha-velocity, simple rotation, flat) chosen by maximum recovered CO flux
key_parameters: dilated mask around spectral peaks at >~3.5 sigma
Halpha mask used for 33 galaxies; rotation mask for 25; flat mask for 2
Halpha spaxels with SNR < 5 excluded from the Halpha mask
assumptions: Halpha mask assumes CO kinematics similar to Halpha; rotation mask assumes a predominantly rotating galaxy with CO spanning the HI velocities

recipe.method: Moment 0, moment 1 and peak-SNR maps from masked cubes; per-spaxel uncertainty from rms of signal-free spectrum times sqrt(N) times channel width; blank pixels outside 2 sigma contour of M0
key_parameters: pixels outside the 2 sigma contour of M0 blanked

recipe.method: Convolve ACA cubes to APEX resolution, take the central-pixel spectrum, correct APEX main-beam efficiency, integrate over a visually defined window and compare with APEX EDGE fluxes

recipe.goal: derive SFR and stellar mass surface density maps from CALIFA
recipe.method: Balmer-decrement extinction per 1 arcsec spaxel, then SFR from extinction-corrected Halpha; stellar mass surface density from PIPE3D maps with dezonification and a Salpeter-to-Kroupa factor of 1.6
key_parameters: correction factor 1.6 from Salpeter (PIPE3D) to Kroupa IMF
assumptions: Cardelli et al. 1989 extinction curve and intrinsic Halpha/Hbeta of 2.86 (case B)

recipe.goal: convert CO intensity to molecular gas surface density
recipe.method: Sigma_mol = (alpha_CO / R21) cos(i) I_CO(2-1) with a constant Milky Way alpha_CO as default; a variable alpha_CO(Z', Sigma_total) as a test
key_parameters: variable alpha_CO computed with Sigma_GMC^100 = 1 and Z' from the CALIFA mass-metallicity relation
assumptions: inclination from an ellipse fit to the SDSS z-band contour at ~1.2 r25, assuming an infinitely thin disk (arccos of axis ratio)

recipe.goal: classify galaxies by Delta SFMS and derive global quantities
recipe.method: Integrate surface densities within r25 for SFR, M*, M_mol; classify as main sequence, green valley or red cloud by Delta SFMS; compare R_mol_star and depletion time between groups
key_parameters: main sequence: Delta SFMS > -0.5 dex; green valley: -1.0 < Delta SFMS <= -0.5 dex; red cloud: Delta SFMS <= -1.0 dex

recipe.goal: measure radial profiles, bulge radii and bulge masses
recipe.method: Average azimuthal CO, stellar and SFR surface densities in elliptical annuli (inclination-corrected) for 30 galaxies; bulge radius from the break in the stellar profile; bulge mass from integrating the stellar profile within R_b
key_parameters: 30 galaxies with i <= 70 deg and 5 sigma integrated CO detections; spaxels with 3 sigma CO detections
annulus width ~5 arcsec (average of minor beam axes)
assumptions: R_b = 1 kpc for spirals without a clear break or with a dominant bar

recipe.goal: fit exponential scale lengths of gas and stars
recipe.method: Fit exponential profiles to the 23 galaxies with decreasing Sigma_mol profiles (stellar fits restricted to disk) and compare l_mol with l_star via an OLS bisector fit y = alpha x
key_parameters: bisector fit for model y = alpha x for main-sequence galaxies with at least 5 sigma l_mol measurements

recipe.goal: fit the resolved SFMS and resolved Kennicutt-Schmidt relations
recipe.method: OLS bisector fits of log Sigma_SFR versus log Sigma_* and log Sigma_mol for main-sequence pixels of the 30 galaxies, compared with CARMA EDGE, PHANGS and ALMaQUEST
key_parameters: pixels from 30 galaxies with 5 sigma global CO detections and i < 70 deg

recipe.goal: compare SFE_mol, molecular-to-stellar fraction and sSFR by Delta SFMS and nuclear activity
recipe.method: Resolved SFE_mol, rR_mol_star and sSFR in bulge pixels and in radial bins, split by Delta SFMS and by nuclear activity (NNA, LINER, AGN); fixed vs variable alpha_CO; Student t-tests on inner vs outer SFE distributions
key_parameters: pixels at r < 0.5 Re rejected for LINER/AGN galaxies to avoid contamination; SFR removed at r < 0.5 Re in profiles
central vs outer split at r = Re for NNA galaxies; r = 1.2 Re for the nuclear-activity comparison
assumptions: Galaxies with no detected nuclear activity are classed as star-forming (SF)

missing_for_reproduction: Mask, noise-model and moment-map software from earlier EDGE work is neither named nor released
PHANGS pipeline settings (line-free channels, image/cell size, cleaning mask parameters) are not listed
SFMS line coefficients, bulge radii breaks, fit procedures and derived-quantity tables are only partly given
Archive project code printed by the paper (2019.2.00029.S) differs from the code the archive links (2019.2.00028.S)
score_reason: ALMA observations and the PHANGS pipeline are public, and many numeric results are given, but CALIFA products, the in-house EDGE masking/moment software, and several imaging settings are not specified.
rediscovery_reason: ACA data of a named project are archived and the imaging recipe is a public pipeline; numeric answer keys exist (flux ratio 0.82, l_mol/l_star = 1.24, slopes 1.20 and 1.19), though CALIFA maps and some steps would need extra sources.
